Python 'İ'.lower() -> 'i'+U+0307 (combining dot), which \w/[^\W_] does not match; regex-tokenizing AFTER str.lower() splits 'İstanbul' into ['i','stanbul']. Match on original/NFC text then lower each token, or allow combining marks. Same \w gap splits Indic words at vowel signs (Mn/Mc).

When reviewing test suites, run quick mutation probes in a /tmp copy (e.g. strip->lstrip, filter-after-slice for top-N with exclusions): surviving mutants reveal spec criteria that tests don't actually discriminate (e.g. large-n stopword tests can't detect stopwords consuming top-N slots).

Parser/validation errors on config files should report line number + reason but NOT echo raw line content (secret leak via logs); test with exact-message asserts so leaks fail tests. Also add commented-out 'KEY=VALUE' lines, tab whitespace, and single-quote/double-double-quote cases to fixtures — reviewers' mutation tests showed naive fixtures miss those regressions.

When testing stateful decorators (retry/backoff, rate-limit, caching), require a test that calls the SAME wrapped function multiple times and asserts per-call state resets; tests that only decorate fresh functions let a 'state hoisted into closure' regression pass. Python: lowercasing before regex tokenizing splits words — 'İ'.lower() == 'i'+U+0307 (combining mark not matched by \w). Run the word regex on NFC original-case text, then lower() each match; normalize stopwords with the same NFC+lower pipeline.

Mutation probes that rewrite a .py module in a loop can get stale __pycache__ bytecode (pyc validated by mtime+size; same-size edits within the same second reuse old code) -> bogus kill/survive results. Run with python3 -B / PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and rm __pycache__.
mutation-testing

Regex word tokenizers: match on NFC original-case text, then lower() each match. Lowering first breaks U+0130 (İ -> i + U+0307 combining mark, a non-\w char) into split tokens. Exhaustive scan confirms U+0130 is the only word char whose lower() contains a non-word char, and no NFC-stable char's lower() is non-NFC or contains an apostrophe.

When the acceptance bar is 'every behavior covered by a test', ask Gerald to mutation-probe the tests in a scratch copy outside the repo: it found that passing tests would also pass on wrong implementations, e.g. edge-apostrophe stripping and stopwords filtered after the top-n slice. Concrete mutants are far stronger evidence than a coverage checklist.

Before writing 'pi install npm:<name>' (or npm publish instructions) in docs, run 'npm view <name>' — the name may already be squatted by an unrelated package, turning the documented command into a silent third-party-code install. agentic-coding on npm is an unrelated Cursor-rules CLI (augmented-os/agentic-coding).

Snapshot/refresh scripts must use sync semantics (clear target dir before copy) not additive copy — pi-config snapshot.sh does rm -rf for skills/ but only additive cp for agents/*.md, so a deleted persona drifts silently (no git status signal). Inconsistent semantics within one script is the smell.

GNU cp -a writes THROUGH destination symlinks by default: backup/restore scripts that cp onto dotfiles-managed symlinks clobber the symlink target, and cp -a of the link as backup preserves only the link, not content. Use cp --remove-destination or lstat/readlink guard. Found in pi-config install.sh.

pi package README/install-command claims can be verified against pi-subagents docs at ~/.pi/agent/npm/node_modules/@tintinweb/pi-subagents/docs/packages.md (install syntax, precedence/shadowing rules) — ground truth for reviewing pi/ packaging changes

Bash backup scripts: never 'cp -a' onto a destination that may be a symlink — it follows the link and overwrites the target. Back up symlinked dests with 'cp -aL' (dereference, preserves content) and install with 'cp -a --remove-destination'. Also guard existence checks as [[ -e f || -L f ]] to catch dangling links under set -e.

Re-review of pi-config c05f4ae: all 12 prior findings verified fixed via /tmp sandbox tests (symlink safety, dangling links, idempotency, secret allowlist). New catch: fix introduced GNU-only flags (cp --remove-destination, date +%N) which break on macOS/BSD; prefer 'rm -f dest && cp -a' and PID-suffixed timestamps for portable bash.

cp -a/-aL with a DIRECTORY destination (or symlink-to-dir) never replaces it: it copies INTO the dir (polluting it) and recurses the whole tree into backups. Guard with explicit -d tests before cp; replace-link logic must handle link-to-dir.

install.sh hardening pattern: guard '[[ -d $dest ]]' FIRST (follows symlinks, catches symlink->dir and real dir) before any backup/copy; use 'rm -f dest && cp -a src dest' instead of GNU-only cp --remove-destination; use timestamp-PID ($$) suffix instead of GNU-only date +%N for portable unique backup dirs; snapshot with cp -aL so the repo never holds absolute symlinks.

Portable bash replacements for GNU-only constructs: 'cp --remove-destination' -> 'rm -f dest && cp -a'; 'date +%N' uniqueness -> '$$' PID suffix; 'rm -f dir/*.glob' (aborts on directory match) -> 'find dir -maxdepth 1 -name pat -type f -delete' (BSD find supports -delete). '[[ -d ]]' follows symlinks, so one guard catches real dirs and symlinks-to-dirs.
pi-config,shell-portability

install-script symlink guards must check EVERY path component, not just the final one: guarding dest with -d/-L only catches final-component symlinks; a parent component (e.g. skills/memory -> /external) still writes through and overwrites pre-existing files outside the target dir, silently, exit 0. Mitigation: realpath dest and assert prefix of realpath target root. Also: snapshot/backup scripts that dereference with cp -aL must apply -L to ALL copy branches (tree copies included) or absolute symlinks leak into the repo and downstream find -type f installs silently skip everything.

pi-config install.sh: parent-component symlinks under AGENT_DIR let installs escape the target dir; guard by realpath -m on dest parent vs realpath -m AGENT_DIR before any backup/copy. -m also handles non-existent AGENT_DIR on first install.

Pattern for guarding parent-component symlink write-through in install scripts: realpath -m the dest's dirname AND the target root, refuse unless parent == root or under root/; place the check AFTER the -d dest guard and BEFORE any backup/copy. -m resolves lexically so it works on first install when the root doesn't exist, and dry-run predicts the refusal for free if placed before dry checks. Verified in pi-config install.sh (commit 0841174).

Job command ['/bin/bash','-c','echo B64 | base64 -d | bash'] makes bash PID1 of a pipeline: SIGTERM from kubelet never reaches the inner script/python (reproduced), so graceful-shutdown handlers are dead code and the container dies by SIGKILL (137) after the grace period. Use exec so the worker is PID1 (or tini). Also Python subprocess reports SIGKILL as returncode -9, not 137.

bash -c 'echo $B64 | base64 -d | exec python3 -' does NOT make python PID 1: exec in the last pipeline stage replaces a forked subshell; bash stays PID 1 and (as PID 1 without handlers) silently drops SIGTERM, so the worker never sees it and is SIGKILLed after grace. Verified with unshare -rpf. Use: exec python3 -c "$(printf %s "$B64" | base64 -d)" (or decode to a file, then exec python3 file).
kubernetes

Job podFailurePolicy rules are first-match in order: a FailJob onExitCodes rule covering the worker's SIGTERM exit code placed before the Ignore onPodConditions DisruptionTarget rule turns every Spot reclaim into a Job failure. Put the DisruptionTarget Ignore rule first. Also with backoffLimit 0 and no matching rule, the Job condition is just BackoffLimitExceeded (no exit code / OOMKilled text) — under MultiKueue that is all the manager sees.

Spot/Kueue watchdogs: Kueue quota admission != node exists. An admitted Job can sit with a Pending pod while the autoscaler finds Spot capacity, and activeDeadlineSeconds/stall timers keep running the whole time. Start stall clocks from a worker-written start/heartbeat marker (or Job status.ready), not from admission or the last per-item status of an earlier attempt. Also make sure in-flight retry counters are not used up by preemptions.
spot

K8s Job failure modes for smoke tests: a bad image tag gives ImagePullBackOff, so the Job stays active and never fails. It only fails via activeDeadlineSeconds, or a watchdog stall rule deletes it. To test a 'failure' classification quickly, use a fast non-zero exit such as bad env leading to exit 3. Job conditions never carry the container OOMKilled reason. Without a podFailurePolicy onExitCodes rule, the Job only shows BackoffLimitExceeded, so a watchdog 'oom' class built on Job conditions is a dead branch.

Plan re-reviews: check that step-dependency statements are true, e.g. 'Steps 1-5 independent' was false when one step base64-embeds another step's file and the CLI step wires two earlier modules. Also, every load-bearing unverified platform assumption (e.g. that MultiKueue copies the FailJob exit-code message to the manager) needs an explicit live-smoke acceptance criterion.

When batch-editing markdown specs with the edit tool, one mismatched oldText rejects the whole batch; verify exact indentation of quoted blocks with sed -n + cat -A before constructing oldText (grep -n context output pads line numbers and hides true indent).

K8s Job gotchas: (1) a plain 'kubectl delete pod' does NOT add the DisruptionTarget condition (only eviction API, preemption, taint-manager, pod GC, kubelet shutdown/pressure do) - so podFailurePolicy Ignore-on-DisruptionTarget cannot be smoke-tested by plain pod delete; use drain/eviction or NoExecute taint. (2) activeDeadlineSeconds clock is stopped/reset while a Job is suspended - Kueue-queued (unadmitted) Jobs never hit DeadlineExceeded; only admitted Jobs do. (3) exit codes not matched by a FailJob onExitCodes rule are invisible from a MultiKueue manager (only BackoffLimitExceeded).

When reviewing a classifier that reads Job conditions, check it against the podFailurePolicy. An exit code that is NOT in a FailJob onExitCodes rule never shows up in a FailJob message, so a rule like 'FailJob carrying exit N' can never match; with backoffLimit 0 the Job just fails with BackoffLimitExceeded. Also, a plain 'kubectl delete pod' does NOT add the DisruptionTarget condition. Eviction, drain, preemption, taint-manager, PodGC and kubelet node-shutdown do. So use drain/eviction or a simulated maintenance event to test an Ignore-on-DisruptionTarget rule.

On this box pytest is NOT installed (python3 -m pytest -> No module named pytest; Python 3.11.2). Plans whose verification is 'python3 -m pytest' must fall back to 'python3 -m unittest' and write tests as unittest.TestCase subclasses; plain pytest-function tests run under unittest discovery silently report 'Ran 0 tests OK' (exit 0) = false pass. Require a parsed non-zero test count.
